Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
915 PM EDT Wed Sep 2 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
The severe weather threat continues to decrease overnight, but the 
threat for thunderstorms remains, especially along and north of I-
66/US-50. Heat Advisories have been issued from 11am to 8pm Thursday 
for portions of the eastern WV Panhandle, southern MD, and 
northern/central VA. 



&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Hot temperatures, high humidity, and severe thunderstorm 
chances look to continue through Friday. 

- 2) Mostly dry conditions and lowering humidity for the Labor
  Day holiday weekend ahead. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Hot temperatures, high humidity, and severe 
thunderstorm chances look to continue through Friday. 

The severe weather threat continues to decrease this evening as the 
the remnant outflow/backdoor front washes out over the region. A 
leftover shower or two has been noted across up across 
Washington/Frederick counties, but this activity has gradually 
decreased in coverage given the stability in the lower levels. 
Scattered to broken mid and high level clouds will remain, 
especially points east of I-81 given the washed out boundary nearby. 

Overall expecting a lull in any activity through at least 2-3am with 
the potential for a secondary round storms dropping south from PA 
heading into early Thursday morning. This activity is currently 
located up across the Twin Tiers of New York/northeast PA where 
numerous severe thunderstorm warnings are in effect. Hi-res guidance 
pushes this activity slowly south into areas along and north of I-
66/US-50 between 2am-6am Thursday morning. Guidance varies on 
coverage with a focus across northern and central MD compared to 
locations further south into Washington DC, southern MD, and 
northern VA. At this rate, not looking at any widespread severe 
weather with this batch of storms although locally gusty winds, 
heavy rainfall, and frequent lightning cannot be ruled out.

The big question is to how this round of morning convection (if it 
occurs) plays into what will happen in the afternoon. Current 
guidance suggest a scattering of storms originating in and around 
the Alleghenies working east as another wave of energy pulses 
through. Some of guidance has limited activity east of the mountains 
while others have more. General consensus is for convection to pop 
toward the mountains and west of US-15 between 11am-2pm before 
working east into the metros between 3-9pm. Coverage remains 
uncertain given any convective debris from the morning. Even with 
that said, expect some organization given 30-35 kts of shear aloft. 
Damaging winds will be the primary threat with storms given 
increased DCAPE values on the order of 1000-1400 j/kg. Large hail 
also cannot be ruled out due to decent lapse rates in the 6-7.5 
degree C/km range. As for flooding, an isolated instance or two 
cannot be ruled out, especially in urban areas or in the event a 
cell backbuilds/trains over a given area. Modeling continues to hold 
additional thunderstorm threats Thursday night into Friday although 
confidence in this is low pending the timing and placement of the 
incumbent cold frontal boundary. 

Right now, most of the guidance has a front dropping through the 
area either Friday morning into Friday afternoon or Friday afternoon 
into Friday night. This would spell continue concerns for severe 
weather in locations along and south of I-70/I-68 where instability 
may be maximized. The added lift from the front should help with 
better coverage and organization of t-storms Friday afternoon and 
evening. Damaging winds will once again be the main threat with 
storms along with frequent lightning, locally heavy rainfall, and 
large hail as secondary concerns. 

Storms will have plenty of fuel to work with as highs pushing back 
into the low to mid 90s Thursday afternoon. Locations south of I-
66/US-50 and along/east of I-95 could see highs in the mid to upper 
90s. Heat indices will range from 100 to 105 degrees for locations 
east of the Blue Ridge. Heat Advisories have been hoisted for 
portions of northern and central VA, southern MD and the eastern WV 
Panhandle where criteria will be met. Baltimore/Washington DC Metros 
will be just shy with heat indices likely hovering in the 100-104 
degree range. Temperatures will cool a bit Friday with highs in the 
upper 80s and low 90s. Heat indices will decrease due to the 
incumbent front, added convection, and increased cloud cover across 
the region. 

KEY MESSAGE 2... Mostly dry conditions and lowering humidity for the 
Labor Day holiday weekend ahead. 

High pressure tracks southeast from the Great Lakes on Saturday, 
pushing a cold front through region throughout the day. Some 
uncertainty still exists regarding how far south this front will 
advance south before stalling, but most ensemble members depict this 
boundary south of our region by Saturday afternoon. This should 
bring a drop in heat & humidity across the Mid-Atlantic, with 
afternoon highs ranging in the mid-80s on Saturday. As mid-level dry 
air continues to track across the area, temperatures should continue 
to decrease as the weekend goes on. By the Labor Day holiday, it 
should feel relatively mild & dry, with dewpoints ranging in the 
upper-50s across the region. 

&&

.AVIATION /01Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...

Overall looking a prevailing VFR to MVFR conditions overnight given 
a washed out boundary nearby. Winds will remain light and variable 
due to the nearby front at less than 10 kts. A shower or 
thunderstorms cannot be ruled out north of a line from MRB/IAD to 
DCA/BWI between 06-10z/2am-6am. Went with PROB30s given the lack of 
confidence in regards to coverage as convection will decaying as it 
moves into the area. 

Additional rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms are possible 
Thursday afternoon through Friday. Expect prevailing VFR conditions 
with temporary restrictions at times. Given low confidence on 
timing, issued PROB30 groups for convection entering the corridor 
west of MRB between 15-19z/11am-3pm before advancing east toward 
IAD, DCA/BWI between 19-00z/2-8pm. Damaging winds will be the 
primary threat with storms along with frequent lightning. Similar 
conditions are expected Friday although timing and coverage remain 
uncertain given the placement of an incumbent cold frontal boundary. 

Prevailing VFR conditions are expected across all terminals for the 
Labor Day holiday weekend. A few showers and thunderstorms Saturday 
afternoon & evening could reduce flight categories south of KCHO. 
Light northwesterly winds on Saturday shift to easterly and calm by 
Sunday evening. VFR conditions look to continue into early next 
week. 
&&

.MARINE...
Overall looking at no marine hazards overnight although 
showers and thunderstorms may sneak into the northern waters 
early Thursday morning. SMWs may be needed as this activity 
drops south although confidence is low. Winds will remain light 
and variable otherwise at less than 10kts. 

SMWS are likely again Thursday afternoon and evening as another wave 
of energy pulses through. Scattered to numerous showers and 
thunderstorms are possible mainly during the 3-9pm timeframe. 

On Friday and Saturday, winds below 15kts most of the time, but 
higher winds and waves could during afternoon and evening showers or 
thunderstorms. SMWS may be needed again to encompass this threat. 
Light northwesterly winds shift easterly by Saturday afternoon as 
the front sags south of the waters and high pressure builds from the 
north. 

&&

.CLIMATE...
Record high minimums were set yesterday at IAD, DCA, and HGR.
Please RERs for detail info. More record high minimums are
possible again tonight and Thursday night.
